newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec budget surplus $19.36 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec budget surplus $19.36 bln.

text.p: The government posted a budget surplus of $19.36 billion in December, the Treasury Department said on Thursday, nearly quadruple the $5.28 billion surplus posted a year earlier in December 1995.
December's surplus followed a November deficit of $37.88 billion.
Total outlays in December were $129.13 billion, down from $135.73 billion in November and down from $133.06 billion in December 1995.
Income or receipts, mostly from taxes, climbed to $148.49 billion in December from $97.85 billion in November and was up from $138.35 billion in December 1995.
During the first three months of fiscal 1997, which ends on Sept 30, the cumulative deficit rose to $58.78 billion from $55.75 billion in the comparable three-month period of fiscal 1996.
December typically is a surplus month because corporations and some individuals make estimated tax payments at year-end.

The flow of revenues was particularly strong in December, possibly reflecting strong corporate profits as well as income gains for individuals from a brisk economy and a strong stock market performance in 1996.
The last published estimate of the government's anticipated fiscal 1997 budget deficit was $125.7 billion, up from a shortfall of $107.28 billion in fiscal 1996.
But a revised fiscal 1997 estimate will be issued when the Clinton administration makes its fiscal 1998 budget presentation to Congress on Feb 6.
